The test image shows a **tomato stem split open longitudinally**, revealing:
- Bleached/white dry internal pith tissue
- Dark grayish-black sclerotia-like structures embedded within the stem cavity
- Brown necrotic outer stem tissue

This strongly suggests **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** — the symptom description specifically mentions "Hard, grayish-black sclerotia about the size of a plump grain of rice embedded within the stem tissue; positive identification achieved by slicing the diseased stem longitudinally."

Now I'll view one reference image to confirm.

The reference image confirms: same disease, same farm setting (black plastic mulch, Bugwood 559384X series). The reference shows external bleached stem with black sclerotia on the surface; the test image shows the stem cut open longitudinally with sclerotia inside and bleached pith — textbook Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot.
